rationale: This is a tiny (909-byte text, 4 functions) numeric compute benchmark dominated by tight floating-point loops (n-body, spectral-norm, partialsums) plus a small recursive kernel, so runtime overhead is the binding constraint while there is ample room to grow size. SUB gets the strongest pull on SecurityGain/DiversityGain because arithmetic-heavy loops are exactly where instruction substitution obscures semantics at near-zero cost; SPLIT is favored for DiversityGain since it composes cheaply with SUB on the few but branch-rich functions (main, recursive). BCF and FLA retain meaningful SecurityGain but carry deliberately elevated RuntimeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights so the selector suppresses them on hot-loop functions where bogus branches and dispatch flattening hurt most, applying them only where features justify it; FLA's CorrectnessRisk is set highest of all because flattening aggressive FP control flow is the most likely pass to perturb this code shape. IBR gets moderate pull as a good security/cost middle ground for the branch-dense main. ICALL and IGV are kept with low-moderate weights because this program has almost no indirect-call or global-variable surface (only four tiny functions, no meaningful call graph to virtualize), so their cost sensitivity dominates their meager benefit. Overall the table biases the selector toward cheap arithmetic/structural transforms and away from expensive control-flow transforms on hot numeric loops.
